mekayis.metin: (قَنَّ) الْقَافُ وَالنُّونُ بَابٌ لَمْ يُوضَعْ عَلَى قِيَاسٍ، وَكَلِمَاتُهُ مُتَبَايِنَةٌ. فَمِنْ كَلِمَاتِهِ الْقِنُّ، وَهُوَ الْعَبْدُ الَّذِي مُلِكَ هُوَ وَأَبُوهُ. وَالْقُنَّةُ: أَعْلَى الْجَبَلِ. وَالْقُنَانُ: رِيحُ الْإِبِطِ أَشَدَّ مَا يَكُونُ. وَالْقُنَاقِنُ: الدَّلِيلُ الْهَادِي، الْبَصِيرُ بِالْمَاءِ تَحْتَ الْأَرْضِ، وَالْجَمْعُ قَنَاقِنُ.

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: قَانُون • (qānūn) m (plural قَوَانِين (qawānīn))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Borrowed from Ancient Greek κᾰνών (kănṓn). Possibly a doublet of قَنَاة (qanāh).
g: axiom, norm, regulation, basic rule, established principle, canon
qanun, kanoon, or ganoun (a musical instrument similar to a zither)

kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Derived from the active participle of قَنَا (qanā, “to reach out to, to acquire”).

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: قَان • (qān) m
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Apparently borrowed from Khorezmian Turkic, from Proto-Turkic *kiān (“blood”).
Unknown, probably an Old South Arabian borrowing, possibly related to قَنَا (qanā), قَنَى (qanā, “to acquire, to obtain”), or to قَنَاة (qanāh, “spear”).
g: a kind of hardwood tree from which bows are made

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: قُنّ • (qunn) m (plural قِنَان (qinān))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Compare the widespread Aramaic ܩܸܢܵܐ / קִנָא / קֵינָא (qennā, “nest; animal burrow; any cluster; family of an animal”), Hebrew קֵן (qēn, “nest”), Akkadian 𒆥𒉡 (qinnu, “nest; lair; family of an animal”). Since this term is spread chiefly in Asiatic Arabic north of Najd, it is probably a continuation of the Aramaic. It is further connected back to Akkadian qanû (“to keep, to buy, to acquire”), itself with relations to Akkadian 𒂵𒈾𒉡 (ganānu, “to confine, especially a person or living thing”), and Akkadian 𒅗𒈾𒉡 (kanānu, “to twist or coil, to wrap up an object or possession”), of Proto-Semitic origin denoting concepts of crafting, to acquire or make, building up, to establish or make stay.
s: Akkadian 𒆥𒉡 (qinnu, “nest; lair; family of an animal”)
Akkadian qanû (“to keep, to buy, to acquire”)
Akkadian 𒂵𒈾𒉡 (ganānu, “to confine, especially a person or living thing”)
Akkadian 𒅗𒈾𒉡 (kanānu, “to twist or coil, to wrap up an object or possession”)
g: coop for domestic birds to be fattened, pen for poultry, brooding cage, henhouse, pigeon’s home and the like

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: قُنّ • (qunn) m
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Uncertain with multiple correlations suggesting doublets of a similar term. A variation of قِمَّة (qimma) denoting a heap or pile, to scrape together into a vertex. Alternatively, a variant of قِنّ (qinn), a clipping of قِنِّينَة (qinnīna); literally a bottle or flask by comparison to its narrowing as it rises. Compare also قُلَّة (qulla) which may have a similar conception as its source or alternative from its smallness at the tip, its narrowing.
g: alternative form of قُنَّة (qunna), summit, small mountain

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: قُنَّة • (qunna) f (plural قُنَن (qunan) or قِنَان (qinān) or قُنُون (qunūn))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Compare قِمَّة (qimma), قُلَّة (qulla), and قُنّ (qunn, “summit, small mountain”), and Inor ቁኒድ (qunīd, “top, summit”)
